name: SeaTable Cloud
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Manage structured records in grids, forms, and simple views

pricing.notes: Typical Plus monthly user amount; vendor may bill in EUR.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 25 users; unlimited bases and tables; 10,000 total rows and 10,000 rows/base; 2 GB storage; 1-month snapshots; 100 Python runs, 3,000 API calls, 100 automations and 12.5 AI credits/month.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 50,000 total rows and 50,000 rows/base; 50 GB storage; 6-month snapshots; per user/month: 250 Python runs, 10,000 API calls, 500 automations and 50 AI credits.
tiers.notes: Vendor publishes €9 monthly or €7 annual; converted at the ECB 2026-07-29 reference rate of €1 = $1.1380. Prices exclude VAT.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited total rows but 100,000 rows/base; 100 GB storage; 12-month snapshots; per user/month: 1,000 Python runs, 50,000 API calls, 5,000 automations and 500 AI credits.
tiers.notes: Vendor publishes €18 monthly or €14 annual; converted at the ECB 2026-07-29 reference rate of €1 = $1.1380. Prices exclude VAT.

tiers.name: Dedicated Cloud
tiers.limits: Minimum 100 users; unlimited total rows but 200,000 rows/base; 1 TB storage; 24-month snapshots; unlimited Python, API, automation and AI usage.
tiers.notes: Annual-only custom EUR quote; prices exclude VAT.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 25 users, unlimited bases/tables, 10,000 total rows, 10,000 rows/base, 2 GB storage, 1-month snapshots, 100 Python runs/month, 3,000 API calls/month, 100 automations/month and 12.5 AI credits/month
pricing.billingTerms: Plus and Enterprise offer monthly + annual billing; Dedicated Cloud is annual only; every team member uses the same plan and billing period
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every team member is billable on a paid team because subscriptions cannot be mixed; row/storage limits block new rows or uploads; bank transfer requires Enterprise annual billing with at least 10 users; Dedicated Cloud has a 100-user minimum; VAT and currency movement are extra.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For SeaTable Cloud, manage structured records in grids, forms, and simple views. The hard boundary is managed collaboration, automations, plugins, storage, and support, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Model structured records, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: managed collaboration, automations, plugins, storage, and support
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for SeaTable Cloud because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: Airtable with fewer ornaments: 3,000 rows, forms, views, automations, and a small app builder for $0.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Baserow's free cloud has a thinner scripting, plugin, and automation environment than SeaTable's mature base extensions and app-building tools.

alternatives.name: Grist
alternatives.desc: A relational spreadsheet with formulas that stays intelligible after column C stops being enough.

facts.install: Hosted signup, desktop app, or Docker container for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Each document is a .grist SQLite database containing table data, attachments, document metadata, and recent history; CSV/Excel exports are also available
facts.gapVsPaid: Grist offers stronger formulas but much less of SeaTable's built-in automation, scripting, form, and app-builder workflow for operational bases.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted or desktop use; shared self-hosting requires Docker, authentication, backups, a public URL, and safe Python-formula sandboxing

alternatives.name: NocoDB Free
alternatives.desc: A managed database grid for three editors and 1,000 records; enough for a small workspace, not a growing one.

facts.dataFormat: Free-plan records and attachments live in NocoDB Cloud; records can be exported through the UI/API, but external database connections are not included on the free plan
facts.gapVsPaid: NocoDB Free has tighter cloud limits and a weaker scripting/app-builder layer than SeaTable for teams building workflows around a managed base.

alternatives.name: SeaTable Free
alternatives.desc: The same managed product, free for 25 users, 10,000 rows, forms, views, automations, scripts, and apps.

facts.dataFormat: Bases live in SeaTable Cloud and can be exported as proprietary .dtable containers containing JSON plus an asset folder; individual tables or views export to XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same service with free-plan limits on rows, storage, automation, and advanced features, so a growing paid workspace will hit the ceiling again.

alternatives.name: Teable Free
alternatives.desc: An Airtable-shaped database with 1,000 rows, 100 automations, and a real app builder on the free plan.

facts.engines: Vendor-hosted AI and App Builder features use Teable's configured model services and free-plan credits; the exact model roster can change
facts.dataFormat: Bases, records, attachments, automation state, and app definitions live in Teable Cloud; bases can be backed up as .tea files and tables exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable's free row allowance and extension ecosystem are smaller, and it cannot match SeaTable's mature scripting and plugin surface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for SeaTable Cloud in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
